title: Rotate the vCenter automation secret without stranding in-flight requests
prompt:
The `VcenterSecretRotation` module rotates the secret of the vCenter automation service account over the vSphere Automation API in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0. The account being rotated is the same account that submits long-running work to vCenter, so a rotation that simply logs in again and drops the previous session abandons whatever that session still owns: the clone that was half-way through is lost, and the operator finds out from a failed inventory rather than from the rotation job.

Make `Invoke-VcenterCredentialRotation` safe to run against a busy vCenter:

* Open a session on the new secret and confirm it belongs to the account being rotated before anything is retired.
* Hold the retiring session open until every request still bound to it has reached a terminal state, polling each one only until it settles.
* Delete the retiring session last, and only once the drain has finished. If the drain does not finish within `-DrainTimeoutSeconds`, report the failure and leave the retiring session alive - a caller can retry a rotation, but work that was abandoned mid-flight cannot be recovered.

Every request has to match `docs/contract.json`, which is transcribed from the OpenAPI document recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. The `wire_rules` section is where this is easy to get wrong: an optional property the caller did not set must be absent from the request rather than present with an empty or null value, and the `spec` parameter of `Cis.Tasks_get` is serialized `style: form, explode: true`.

Keep the exported function name and its parameter names as they are.

Verify with `./run_tests.sh`. The contents of `tests/`, `docs/` and `run_tests.sh` are fixtures - do not modify them.
environment_note: Verification is fully offline: it generates a throwaway loopback certificate, starts tests/mock/vcenter_contract_mock.py on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port, and asserts the request log the mock writes. No VMware endpoint is contacted.
capability_objective: Implement a REST client whose request wire shape matches a specification-derived contract exactly, including omitting unset optional properties, while getting the ordering of a credential rotation right so in-flight work is not stranded on the retiring session.
